LESSON: LOCOMOTIVE MOTOR SKILLS

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: BASIC
Topic 10.1: Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which activity do you MOTOR skills learner should be able to; catch, climb and slide. enjoy most?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya
3. practise Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in clear steps
4. apply Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LOCOMOTIVE MOTOR SKILLS
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: LOCOMOTIVE MOTOR SKILLS
Study Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which activity do you MOTOR skills learner should be able to; catch, climb and slide. enjoy most?
2. How do you climb and response • Encourage learners to throw slide?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Locomotive MOTOR SKILLS from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
